description: A Trie is a tree where each path from the root spells out a prefix of some inserted string, letting insert/search/prefix-check run in O(L) time (L = word length) regardless of how many words are stored — far better than scanning a list of strings.
important_details: Each node holds children (commonly a 26-size array for lowercase letters, or a HashMap for larger alphabets) and an 'isEndOfWord' flag.
Prefix queries (startsWith) are the trie's superpower — no other structure answers 'does any word start with X' this efficiently.
Combines naturally with DFS/backtracking for grid word-search problems (prune search paths that aren't valid prefixes).
A bitwise trie (storing binary representations of numbers) unlocks O(32) or O(64) max-XOR-pair queries.
other_relevant_details: Recognize the pattern from phrases like 'prefix', 'starts with', 'autocomplete', 'dictionary of words', or repeated prefix lookups against a fixed word list.

variations.description: The foundational trie supporting three operations: insert a word, check if an exact word exists, and check if any word has a given prefix.
important_details: insert() walks/creates nodes for each character, marking isEndOfWord=true only at the final character.
search() must check isEndOfWord at the final node; startsWith() does NOT — reaching the node is sufficient.
A failed traversal (child doesn't exist) short-circuits both search and startsWith to false immediately.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(L) per operation (L = word/prefix length). Space: O(total characters inserted * 26) worst case.

problems.name: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure

variations.variation: Word Search II (Trie + Backtracking on Grid)
variations.description: Search a 2D letter grid for multiple dictionary words simultaneously by building a trie of all target words first, then doing one combined DFS/backtracking pass that prunes any path not matching a trie prefix.
important_details: Building a single trie of all words lets one DFS pass find all matches, instead of running a separate DFS per word (which would be O(words * cells * 4^L)).
Mark cells visited during DFS by temporarily mutating the grid (e.g., to '#'), then restore on backtrack.
An optimization: remove a word from the trie (or mark its node) once found, to avoid duplicate results and prune further search.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(rows*cols*4^L) worst case, but trie pruning makes it far faster in practice. Space: O(sum of word lengths) for the trie.

variations.description: A trie built over the binary representation of numbers (bit by bit, MSB to LSB) enabling O(32) queries for the maximum XOR pair or the max XOR of a number against a growing set.
important_details: At each node, greedily try to descend into the OPPOSITE bit of the query number to maximize the XOR at that position.
Fixed depth of 32 (or 31/64 depending on constraints) regardless of how many numbers are stored — this is what makes it faster than brute-force O(n^2) pairwise XOR.
Insert every number into the trie first (as a preprocessing step) before running queries against it.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(n * 32) to build, O(32) per query. Space: O(n * 32) nodes worst case.

variations.description: Use a trie to efficiently support prefix-based suggestions (autocomplete) or to accelerate dictionary lookups inside a DP/backtracking word-segmentation problem.
important_details: For autocomplete, DFS from the prefix's end node collecting all complete words below it (often combined with a frequency count for ranking).

For Word Break, a trie of dictionary words lets the DP transition check 'does s[j..i] exist in dictionary' in O(L) instead of a hashset lookup with string-slicing overhead — mainly a performance optimization over the standard HashSet-based DP.
Storing top-k suggestions at each trie node (precomputed) trades space for O(k) query time instead of a DFS per query.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: A true trie-DFS approach is O(prefix length + matches found) per query. Space: O(total characters across all words).
